name: Howmet Aerospace
description: Howmet makes the hard-to-make metal parts inside aircraft engines and airframes: turbine blades and vanes (investment castings), forged rings, aerospace fasteners, titanium mill products and structures, plus forged aluminum truck wheels. Most of its sales go to a few engine and aircraft makers (RTX and GE Aerospace were each about 11 percent of 2025 third-party sales), under long-term programs, and a large slice is spare parts for engines already flying. About 53 percent of 2025 sales were commercial aerospace, 17 percent defense, 11 percent industrial gas turbines (power generation) and only 15 percent commercial transportation. Segment EBITDA margins of 21 to 33 percent in 2025 reflect scarce capacity and pricing power.

businessLines.name: Engine Products
businessLines.how: Engine makers buy parts under long-term contracts and programme awards for new engines, plus recurring aftermarket spares as engines are overhauled; price and volume rise with engine build rates and gas turbine demand.
businessLines.description: Investment castings (airfoils) and seamless rolled rings for aircraft engines and industrial gas turbines, including rotating parts and structural castings.

revenue.note: Third-party sales; FY2024 $3,735M. Q2 2026 segment third-party sales $1,373M vs $1,038M.

operatingProfit.note: Segment Adjusted EBITDA (the company's segment measure); FY2024 $1,150M (30.8 percent). Share of $2,507M total segment adjusted EBITDA (computed).

businessLines.name: Fastening Systems
businessLines.how: Airframe and engine makers and distributors buy fasteners per part in high volumes under supply contracts; installation tools and replacement fasteners add repeat sales.
businessLines.description: Aerospace and industrial fastening systems, commercial transportation fasteners and installation tools.

businessLines.name: Engineered Structures
businessLines.how: Aerospace and defense makers buy titanium forgings and structures per part under multi-year contracts; vertically integrated from ingot to machined part.
businessLines.description: Titanium ingots and mill products; titanium forgings, extrusions and machining for airframe, wing and aero-engine applications.

businessLines.name: Forged Wheels
businessLines.how: Truck and trailer makers and fleets buy wheels per unit; demand follows heavy-truck build cycles (10-K expects commercial transportation demand to stay low).
businessLines.description: Lightweight forged aluminum wheels for trucks, buses and trailers, sold under the Alcoa Wheels brand.
